Synopsis:
    The Fed's Inspector General has issued a report calling for an overhaul of governance processes surrounding the selection of regional Fed bank presidents and oversight of Class C directors. Key deficiencies identified include lack of pre-screening for financial conflicts of interest among Class C directors, absence of formal documentation of candidate selection procedures across Reserve Banks, and inconsistent practices between regional banks. The Board of Governors has concurred with the IG's recommendations and committed to remedial actions. The focus is entirely on institutional governance reform, not monetary policy.
